root_cause.text: The error handling path in xhci_disable_slot() uses kfree() to free only the command structure, but xhci_alloc_command() allocates both a command structure and a completion structure when called with a true second argument, leaving the completion structure unfreed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces two instances of `kfree(command)` with `xhci_free_command(xhci, command)` in the error paths of xhci_disable_slot(). The commit message explicitly states that "xhci_alloc_command() allocates a command structure and, when the second argument is true, also allocates a completion structure" and that "xhci_free_command() correctly frees both the command structure and the associated completion structure," whereas the original code only freed the command structure itself, causing the completion structure to leak.

candidates.rationale: This kfree() call at line 4149 only frees the command structure itself, but xhci_alloc_command() was called with a true second argument which allocates both a command structure AND a completion structure. Using kfree() directly bypasses the proper cleanup logic in xhci_free_command() that would free both allocated resources, causing a memory leak of the completion structure.

This kfree() call at line 4157 has the same issue as line 4149 - it only frees the command structure but not the completion structure that was allocated by xhci_alloc_command(). This is an error handling path where the command allocation succeeded but a subsequent operation failed, leaving the completion structure unfreed.
